text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - Network egress degradation detected in azure canadacentral. Private/VPN-connected customers reporting increased latency and occasional TCP timeouts. Incident created (2098765432). Paging oncall-ops.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created (severity P1). Auto-triage: potential BGP/routing instability affecting vnet-to-onprem egress.

oncall-ops: ack. @netops-sam @infra-alyssa @sre-jordan please triage. Bridge: #inc-2098765432-call.

netops-sam: seeing a route preference flip on our edge peers in canadacentral. Several prefixes that normally prefer our peered metro are now advertised with higher MED/metric and are being chosen via a longer path. Spikes in egress latency and retransmits.

infra-alyssa: confirming, CloudWatch-like metrics (our collector) show egress p95 latency for canadacentral private prefixes from 120ms -> 420ms around 2098765400. Packetloss visible to a subset of customers.

sre-jordan: quick customer impact check: two paying Dedicated customers with on-prem VPNs having increased request failures to private endpoints. No broad API outage for hosted customers yet.

netops-sam: raw BGP snippet: 
```
# show bgp neighbors advertised-routes
Prefix: 203.0.113.0/24  next-hop 10.1.1.1 med 200 localpref 100
Previously: med 20
```
Looks like Azure edge started honoring a changed MED from a partner fabric. Possibly regression in route selection after their Friday rollout.

infra-alyssa: I opened a ticket with Azure support (INCIDENT-#987654). They say they saw a partial control-plane rollout in canadacentral that affects MED handling. Support assigned to network ops on their end. ETA 20-30m for rollback.

azure-support: Thanks for the report. We've identified a control-plane change in canadacentral that altered MED precedence for some routes. We're rolling back the change to affected edge routers now. Rolling back to stable config across 6 PoPs, starting with the busiest. Will update in ~10m.

eng-bridges: temporary mitigation: we're enabling fallback routing for Private customers to force egress via our dedicated secondary peering in us-central for affected prefixes. This will increase egress cost for some customers but reduce latency. Patching routing policy now.

deploy-bot: Routing policy patch queued: canary -> 10% of flows to us-central, 100s probe windows. Will auto-promote if health checks pass.

oncall-ops: handoff plan: @sre-jordan will stay through mitigation, I'll be available for postmortem. If rollback completes, we stand down.

netops-sam: Applied temporary AS-PATH prepend on our peer advertisements for the affected prefixes to de-preference the bad path. Command used on our side: 
```
az network vnet-gateway update --name gw-canadacentral --resource-group infra-rg --set bgpSettings.asPathPrepend="65001 65001"
```
This forces preferencing back to our primary egress.

customer-success-maya: notifying impacted customers on the Concierge list. Message drafted and sent to 3 customers. Flagging any escalations here.

azure-support: rollback applied to 4/6 edge devices. Early telemetry shows prefix selection reverting. Continuing rollout to remaining devices.

sre-jordan: running synthetic checks to customer VPNs and private endpoints — pings and TCP handshakes returning to baseline for 80% of test prefixes. Error rates dropping: 12% -> 1.8% in the last 3 minutes.

netops-sam: BGP convergence looks stable now. No new MED flips in the last 3 minutes.

oncall-ops: mitigation observed. Keeping incident open for monitoring window (15m).

eng-bridges: canary promotion to 100% completed for fallback routing. No adverse effects observed.

azure-support: rollback complete across all targeted edges. We will open a follow-up RCA with timestamps and affected device list.

sre-jordan: confirmed end-to-end customer tests good. Marking degraded -> mitigated.

oncall-ops: Incident mitigated at 2098765445. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-04-02 16:00 UTC in #postmortems. Action items: (1) evaluate permanent routing policy to avoid single-control-plane regressions, (2) add automatic fallback to secondary peering in runbook, (3) follow up with Azure for SLA credit paths.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 status changed to RESOLVED by oncall-ops at 2098765450.

oncall-ops: :thumbsup: thanks team. Will collect logs and timeline and drop raw artifacts into the incident doc.

customer-success-maya: sending final customer update: "Issue mitigated, services restored, we will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

pagerduty-bot: Incident closed.
